Implementations of signal, locked signal, timeout wait, RCU reference acquire and reference release helpers and their wakeup and lifetime contracts.
Contents and behaviour of array and chain operations tables and lifetime rules for container fences.
Real DMA mapping, allocation, synchronization and mask handling when DMA support is enabled, including scatter list and IOVA allocation paths.

findings.text: Provides a helper that obtains a stable counted reference from a RCU protected fence pointer, returning null when empty and otherwise looping until the observed pointer still matches after acquiring the reference, dropping mismatched acquisitions and retrying indefinitely.

Fence mutual exclusion uses either an embedded spinlock or an external spinlock chosen by an inline lock flag; interrupt saving lock and unlock helpers operate on the selected lock, and a debug assertion verifies the selected lock is held by the caller.
Signalling scope helpers are inert in these fragments: beginning signalling always reports success while ending signalling and the might wait hook have no observable effect.

Signalled determination first consults a signalled flag for immediate true, otherwise under RCU protection consults an optional driver callback and on positive indication promotes the fence to signalled through the locked or unlocked signal path before reporting true.

Sequence ordering compares two numbers either as full wide values when a wide flag is set or as signed difference of their low halves otherwise, so the latter tolerates wrap while the former requires strict greater than.

Later comparisons require identical fence contexts and warn and fail when contexts differ; equality plus later defines later or same, and selection of the later fence returns null when contexts differ or when the winning fence is already signalled, otherwise the winning unsignalled fence.

Locked status reports zero while unsignalled and otherwise the stored error or one on success; error may only be set before signalling with a negative errno range; timestamp waits for a timestamp valid flag after signalling and substitutes current time when queried prematurely.
Blocking wait maps an unbounded timeout wait onto zero on success or negative restart result, preserving negative outcomes and normalizing any non negative outcome to success.
Container classification identifies array fences and chain fences by identity of their operations table against dedicated global tables, with container meaning either array or chain.

DMA mapping operations table is a collection of optional method pointers covering coherent allocation and release, page based allocation, mapping of physical ranges and scatter lists, synchronization for CPU and device in single and scatter list forms, cache synchronization, address mask queries, mapping size hints and merge boundary, plus mmap and scatter table retrieval.
Device operations accessor either prefers a per device table with architecture fallback and stores a supplied table, or in the alternate configuration always yields null on lookup and ignores stores.

In the fallback configuration contiguous and CMA helpers report absence with null, false or not supported, coherent declaration reports not supported with zero valued allocation mapping and release helpers and empty release, global coherent allocation reports null with zero valued release and mapping, while the generic contiguous free helper releases pages by order.

Coherence and bounce determination treats devices as coherent either by querying device state or unconditionally true with a true default, clears a skip sync flag at most once on the hot path, considers small allocation bounce unnecessary when bounce handling is disabled or when coherent or device bound, requires sufficiently large or suitably aligned sizes for direct use, and requests bounce only when both safety and alignment fail.

Architecture DMA hooks for synchronization, preparation, setup, teardown and debug bus registration are empty in these fragments, direct mapping and allocation predicates all report false, and page protection conversion either forces non cached or leaves protections unchanged.

DMA attribute bits occupy distinct powers of two: weak ordering bit one, write combine bit two, no kernel mapping bit four, skip CPU sync bit five, force contiguous bit six, alloc single pages bit seven, no warn bit eight, privileged bit nine, MMIO bit ten, debugging ignore cachelines bit eleven, require coherent bit twelve, CC shared bit thirteen and internal alloc CC shared bit fourteen.

Mapping failure is signalled by an all ones DMA address, bit mask helper denotes low n bits set, IOVA swiotlb marker is the top bit of a wide size field, header include guards use their respective macro names, and default coherent is true.

IOVA progress state holds a DMA address plus a packed size word whose top bit flags swiotlb use; usable size masks out that flag with truncation safe for narrow systems, and IOVA use is defined as nonzero packed size.

When DMA mapping support is absent the mapping layer provides inert fallbacks: page, physical and resource maps report the mapping error sentinel, scatter map reports zero, scatter table map reports operation not supported, unmaps do nothing, allocation returns null, frees do nothing, table and mmap retrieval report not present, capability checks report false, mask setting reports IO error, required mask and sizes and merge boundary report zero, noncontiguous allocation and virtual mapping return null with empty free and invalid mmap.

Mapping error detection either invokes a debug hook then reports out of memory exactly when the address equals the error sentinel or in the alternate fallback unconditionally reports out of memory; debug mapping hooks are empty; cache alignment is an architecture minimum when defined else one.

Holding a RCU acquired fence reference without revalidating the source pointer risks referencing a reallocated object under reuse allocators, so equality recheck before handoff is mandatory; spinning for timestamp validity can busy wait if signalling omits the timestamp flag; setting error after signalling or with out of range values and comparing fences from different contexts indicate driver misuse.
DMA page mapping, coherent allocation and mask configuration entry points covered here exhibit the absent support fallback contracts of error sentinel, null allocation and IO error respectively.
